sources.ref: Walkplay Android app 2.3.1 (com.ttgk.musicbox): the KT register EQ screen (what an apply and a save send) and its filter type list

meta.notes: Walkplay's own app drives SchemeNo19 as a KT Micro register device, not with the Walkplay protocol: 6 bands from register 0x35, each band a gain register (s16 dB x 10, then the frequency in whole Hz) and a Q register (u16 x 1000, then the type), the same layout as Kiwi Ears and Tanchjim. The type byte is the type code plus 8 (bit 3 always set), and the app masks it with 7 on a read. The app writes register 0x34 with a 1 after the bands, where Kiwi Ears' firmware takes it first; that register is also the EQ switch there. Each write waits up to a second for the device's answer, and the app carries on whatever comes back. A save adds the commit. The bridge does the same, and also writes the DAC offset slider as the Global Gain control: register 0x57 holding minus ten times the dB, -12 to 0 dB in 0.1 dB steps. The editor offers peaking, high shelf, low shelf, high pass and low pass, 20 to 20000 Hz, gain +/-10 dB in 0.1 dB steps and Q 0.1 to 5 (typed as a decimal, 0.001 on the wire), with no pre-gain besides the DAC offset. These are the app's editor limits, and nothing here is confirmed on a device. The bridge does not write the register where the app records which of its own presets is selected (0x16); we have no meaningful index to put there, so the app may show a stale selection after a push. The app has no EQ off switch for these devices; the bridge can still write 0 to register 0x34, which is how Kiwi Ears' KT firmware turns its EQ off. devicePEQ differs: it drives this scheme with its Walkplay handler (6 bands, peaking and shelves, +/-10 dB). Out of scope: the app's microphone (ADC) EQ and ADC gain register 0x3a, and a flash erase command.
